source_refs.note: Absorption and Emission Spectra: a main subheading of 18.7 Atomic Spectra, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 130-131.

blocks.text: When light with a continuous spectrum such as white light is passed through a gas at low pressure, and spectrum of light is then analysed, it is found that light of certain wavelengths is missing. In their places dark lines are seen. This type of spectrum is called absorption spectrum. As the light passes through the gas, electrons absorb discrete amount of energy and make transition to higher energy levels. Only photons of certain energy or frequency are absorbed. The wavelengths of light absorbed correspond exactly to energy needed to make such upward transitions. When these excited electrons return to lower levels, the photons are emitted of specific wavelengths given out in emission spectrum. It means the wavelengths missing from an absorption line spectrum are those present in the emission line spectrum as shown in Fig. 18.13.

blocks.alt: Three strips on a 400 to 750 nm scale: (a) the continuous spectrum, a full band of colours from violet to red; (b) the hydrogen emission spectrum, bright lines at about 410, 434, 486 and 656 nm on black; (c) the hydrogen absorption spectrum, the colour band with dark lines at the same wavelengths.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.13: Relation between an absorption spectrum and the emission spectrum of the same element: (a) spectrum of white light, (b) emission spectrum of element, (c) absorption spectrum of the same element (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.13).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed caption of Figure 18.13 swaps (b) and (c): (b) is the emission spectrum and (c) the absorption spectrum, as captioned above. Its wavelength scale is printed 400 ... 650, 650, 700; the scale runs from 400 to 750 nm, as drawn above.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: Photon must have energy exactly equal to the energy difference between the two shells for excitation of an atom but an electron with K.E. greater or equal can excite the gas atoms. This transition of energy is equl to; hf = Eₙ − Eₚ.

blocks.alt: Three horizontal strips. Continuous spectrum: an unbroken band of colour from violet through blue, green, yellow and orange to red. Line spectrum: a black strip with four separate bright lines, violet, blue, green and red. Band spectrum: the coloured band crossed by dark lines at the same four places.
blocks.caption: For your information: Different types of spectra: continuous spectrum, line spectrum and band spectrum (original drawing after the textbook's For your information box).
